newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks settle down by noon as bonds dip.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks settle down by noon as bonds dip.

text.p: SPI Futures 2490 -6 US 30yr cl 6.96 -0.02
10yrbond futs 92.080 -0.055 Gold NY 339.55 Lon fix 340.15
*Stocks settle modestly lower by midsession after February quarter wages data pressures markets. Volume 169.13 million, A$309.36 million, 786 stocks traded, 288 steady, 234 up, 264 down.
A slow Australian share market settled modestly lower by the midsession on Thursday after bond markets dipped on stronger than expected local wages data.
By 12.05 p.m. (0200 GMT), the benchmark All Ordinaries index was 4.7 points lower at 2,483.3.
June share price index futures were down six points at 2,490, a 6.7 point premium to the underlying index.

Bond markets scarpered lower after the data showed an increase in average weekly ordinary time earnings of 1.3 percent in the February quarter and 4.6 percent annually, compared to economists forecasts of 0.8 percent and 3.9 percent.

"The wages numbers knocked the bonds about and we have seen some follow through in our market," said a dealer at a Perth-based brokerage, adding that the general consolidative tone of the day had failed to surprise in any case.
"I wasn't really expecting much today. We had our rush of blood yesterday."

Among the leaders, miners CRA and WMC were worst affected, both striking light selling as profit takers cashed in some of their recent gains. CRA was down 20 cents at A$18.92 with weakness in sister entity RTZ Plc not helping, while gold/nickel miner WMC lost 10 cents to A$7.50.
Among others, drug developer Cortecs International, added 22 cents to A$5.82, albeit in thin trade, as it awaited the results of its 'Macritonin' osteoporosis treatment, due by May 2.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about 10 to nine, while about 37 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
In other local markets, short Australian debt futures fell sharply after the jump in first quarter wages pushed the annual rate through the RBA's perceived comfort zone of 4.5 percent.
By 12.35 p.m. (0235 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.93 percent, up 0.08 from Wednesday's levels.
The Australian dollar leapt 1/4 cent to clear tough US$0.7830 resistance by noon after the wages data seemed to put paid to the risk of a rate cut, at least in the short term.
By 12.15 pm (0215 GMT) the dollar had leapt to US$0.7837/42 from an early US$0.7808/13 and US$0.7813/18 late here Wednesday.
